title: qu'est-ce qui vs qu'est-ce que - Master 'What' Questions
description: THE BIGGEST distinction in French questions: qu'est-ce qui (what DOES - subject) vs qu'est-ce que (what DO you - object). Master this, ask anything!
can_do: Ask 'What does X?' vs 'What do you?' correctly
Form perfect questions in any situation

vocabulary.note: SUBJECT question - thing is doing the shining
SUBJECT question - thing is doing the falling
SUBJECT question - thing is making noise
SUBJECT question - thing is making grass green
OBJECT question - you are seeing WHAT
OBJECT question - you are eating WHAT
OBJECT question - birds are eating WHAT

concepts.definition: qu'est-ce qui = what DOES something (subject). qu'est-ce que = what DO you verb (object)
concepts.example: {Qu'est-ce qui brille?} (What shines? - subject) vs Qu'est-ce que tu vois? (What do you see? - object)

concepts.definition: Use QUI when asking WHAT is doing the action. No other subject after qui!
concepts.example: {Qu'est-ce qui brille?} (What shines?), {Qu'est-ce qui fait du bruit?} (What makes noise?), {Qu'est-ce qui rend l'herbe verte?} (What makes grass green?)

concepts.definition: Use QUE when asking what someone/something DOES TO something. Subject comes after que!
concepts.example: {Qu'est-ce que tu vois?} (What do you see?), {Qu'est-ce que tu manges?} (What are you eating?), {Qu'est-ce que le soleil fait?} (What does the sun do?)

concepts.definition: If 'what' is the subject (no other subject follows) → {qui}. If another subject follows → {que}.

concepts.term: Transform ANY Statement into a Question
concepts.definition: You can now ask 'what' questions about anything you've learned!
concepts.example: {Le soleil brille} → {Qu'est-ce qui brille?} (What shines?), {Je vois un oiseau} → {Qu'est-ce que tu vois?} (What do you see?)

mistakes.feedback: Use {qu'est-ce qui} here: 'what' is the subject, and no other subject follows. Use {qu'est-ce que} when another subject follows.
Use '{qu'est-ce QUI}' when asking what DOES something (subject). The thing itself is doing the shining - that's the subject!
Use '{qu'est-ce QUI}' for subject questions. The thing itself is falling - it's the subject, not an object!
Perfect causative question! But use '{qu'est-ce QUI}' because the subject (what) is DOING the action of making grass green.

items.hint: qu'est-ce que + tu vois (you see WHAT)

mistakes.feedback: Use '{qu'est-ce QUE}' when asking what you DO to something (object). You see SOMETHING. That something is the object. QUI = subject, QUE = object.
Use '{qu'est-ce QUE}' for object questions. You are seeing WHAT - that's the object of your seeing!
Use '{qu'est-ce QUE}' for object questions. You are eating WHAT - the food is the object!
